summary: Prepare a verified Coolify Compose deployment using existing application Docker targets, without changing React, API, worker or business logic.
acceptance: Existing web/api/worker image targets build from the repository root with no application-source or Dockerfile changes.
Production Compose starts all three processes and private PostgreSQL/Redis/S3 with stable generated credentials, persistent named volumes, healthchecks and fail-closed required environment.
Web routes /api to api:3000 on the shared resource network; only web receives the public HTTPS domain on internal8080, with application auth URLs using public origin without8080.
Database migrations complete before API is healthy and before worker starts; restarts retain schema/data/bucket and do not rotate secrets.

Actual image builds and production-container smoke prove web/API proxy, database migrations/readiness, authenticated queue worker and private S3. Existing quality and48HTTP regressions remain enabled.

User guide names the real existing Compose path, exact Coolify fields, short APP_URL/SMTP inputs and generated service credentials, distinguishing prepared config from actual server/TLS/SMTP/backups acceptance.
Proxy accepts valid uploaded PDFs above1MiB while application retains its10MiB authority; configuration change only, original application source unchanged.
Nginx resolves the API service after independent API recreation without requiring a frontend code/image change; startup DNS is not treated as permanent.
semanticRouting: Deployment-only scope changes service orchestration, secrets, networking, persistent storage, migration ordering and CI. Existing business rules, document processing, application auth/roles and UI are preserved. Architecture/security consult precedes implementation; platform implements and independent architecture/QA review actual config and CI.

findings.summary: Default nginx1MiB cap rejected PDFs allowed by API
findings.resolution: Proxy now allows11m while application preserves10MiB. Independent source review and actual >1MiB authenticated upload/extraction/download checksum passed production CI.

findings.summary: Redis shell command bypassed image privilege drop
findings.resolution: Explicit Redis image user configured; architecture independently reread and actual startup/authenticatedqueue/AOF volume persistence passed.

findings.summary: Static nginx upstream could retain an obsolete API address after independent replacement
findings.resolution: Shared upstream zone with Docker resolver and resolve supported in nginx1.28, independently reread. Real API-only replacement preserved nginx identity/start time and proxy worked; addresses were reused, so changed-IP recovery remains an explicit unforced scenario limit.

limitations: No live server MCP tools are exposed. No remote server deployment, provisioned certificate, actual SMTP delivery, deployed-browser E2E, offsite backup or restore is certified.
This closes production configuration readiness only; full Phase5 still requires user-server operational acceptance. Single host is not high availability.
Production smoke uses isolated synthetic identity/data and configured HTTPS cookie semantics over internal HTTP; no real TLS ingress or external mail.
API recreation preserved its network addresses in CI; forced web-facing IP change was not exercised. DNS configuration was independently reviewed and actual nginx startup/proxy recreation passed.
CPU/memory/PID defaults are bounded pilot settings, not capacity benchmarks; existing build-stage runtime retains dev dependencies by unchanged Dockerfile design.
independenceRationale: Production secrets, persistent commercial data, migration sequencing and public ingress require independent security/architecture and actual-service QA before readiness is verified.
